title: The Smell That Made Parliament Want To Leave
description:
In the hot summer of 1858 the River Thames, filled with untreated sewage, smelled so terrible that London's Parliament soaked its curtains in chloride of lime and discussed moving out of town. Disraeli was reported leaving a committee room with a handkerchief over his nose. The Great Stink pushed Parliament to let the city borrow £3 million, and engineer Joseph Bazalgette built a new sewer system using 318 million bricks. It still works today.

Source: Wikipedia, 'Great Stink'.
